[h1][b]🎮 Reseña de STAR WARS™ Galactic Battlegrounds Saga[/b][/h1]

[h2]Resumen del Juego[/h2]
STAR WARS™ Galactic Battlegrounds Saga es básicamente el “¿y si Age of Empires, pero con blásters?” que muchos pedían y pocos admiten que siguen jugando. Es estrategia en tiempo real con construcción de bases, recolección de recursos y ese ritmo de “un aldeano más y ahora sí ataco”… hasta que te cae un ejército y recuerdas que la diplomacia no existe en la galaxia.

La parte “Acción” no es de gatillo rápido: es la acción de ver cómo tus tropas se derriten en tiempo real mientras tú microgestionas como si fueras un almirante… con mouse tembloroso. Primera impresión: un clásico 2D con encanto retro, mucho sabor a ciencia ficción, y suficiente caos para arruinar amistades en multijugador (lo cual, seamos honestos, es parte del canon).

[h2]Lo Bueno y lo No Tan Bueno del Lado de la Fuerza[/h2]

Lo Bueno:
✅ 🏗️ Construcción de bases y economía clásica: simple, adictiva y peligrosa para tu horario de sueño.  
✅ ⚔️ Estrategia en tiempo real con combates constantes: siempre hay algo explotando (o a punto de).  
✅ 🌌 Ambientación Star Wars bien marcada: unidades, facciones y “vibes” espaciales que venden la fantasía.  
✅ 🎶 Gran banda sonora: sí, esto ayuda a sentirte importante incluso cuando estás perdiendo.  
✅ 🧑‍🤝‍🧑 Multijugador y JcJ + Remote Play Together: ideal para discutir quién “jugó sucio” desde el minuto 3.

Lo No Tan Bueno:
❌ 🏆 Cero logros: Steam te mira y dice “¿orgullo y satisfacción? aquí no”. 😶  
❌ 👥 Comunidad activa pequeña (158 jugadores): encontrar rivales puede sentirse como buscar jedis después de la Orden 66.  
❌ 🎥 Presentación 2D de clásico: encantadora… hasta que tu nostalgia se acaba y quieres algo más moderno. 🧱  
❌ 🧠 Si vienes por “Acción” tipo shooter, aquí la acción es ver barras de vida bajar con disciplina militar. 🔫➡️🗺️  
❌ 🕹️ El multijugador puede volverse una religión de veteranos: entras “casual” y sales bautizado por el fuego. 🔥

Star Wars Battlegrounds is a chaotic and unintentionally hilarious experience I would recommend to anyone. Though it may be an Age of Empires clone, i feel it does stand on its own, even against its successor in the RTS community (Empire at War). Nostalgia aside, I keep coming back to this game. Its map editor and custom campaign creator were revolutionary in '01. The best you could do in prior games was imagine a story with the maps one had created, but here, you can write your own objectives, code them to work, and write in scenario instructions, as though it were real. 

Now, I will be honmest, I haven't played the campaign in years. The custom campaigns are just so much fun to create. I also use map reveal and insta build. So, my view may be a bit skewed. I heard the modding community bolsters this game from good to great, but I can't comment on that, as I haven't tried them.

All in all, I highly recommend it, even if the intro cutscenes weren't updated for modern systems (Come on, guys. If an obscure game like Outwars can get the cutscene fix treatment. So, can this juggernaught). The only issue I ever had with it was the infamous crashing at random points. Some days its fine, others, it crashes shortly after the music ends. Even so, I give a thumbs up and recommend it wholeheartedly.

Would I recommend it above EAW? The supposed best Star Wars RTS, as said by Petroglyph themselves? Well, It has a few short comings to it that make it fall just a bit short. Apart from the crashing, it has very lazy skirmish AI, and space battles tend to be a slog if you are too far from the enemy base. However, the chaotic factor when two armies clash is unique to this game (in Star Wars RTS, I mean). So, while not as good, it has twice the fun. (No, I am not going to attack the older graphics vs EAW's 3D rendering. A lot of game tech improvement happened in those 5 years, and budgets were a factor. It wouldn't be fair to judge based solely on looks, or the newer one would win every time). 

Thanks for reading.

As a child, I played this game very often. It was still fun for a decent amount of time after trying it out as an adult. Nothing is to scale so a lot of units look goofy, like Geonosian warriors being the same size as Jedi starfighters. Functionally each faction is completely the same, with the exception of some exclusive research perks and some tech/unit restrictions imposed during the story.

Most of what made it so fun to replay was all of the expanded universe content, especially the stuff introduced while Episode 2 was still new. That time between the release of Episodes 2 and 3 brought a lot of interesting things, like Arc Troopers, several other games and the 2d Clone Wars shorts. The Clone Wars campaigns feature the characters Sev'Rance Tann and Echuu Shen Jon, introduced in this game who, lore-wise make up small articles on wookiepedia, but have an enjoyable journey for you to play though. 

Without nostalgia, this game would probably be very boring compared to other games like Empire at War, which is better in every way and the myriad of other available games that come on sale regularly. Though  I believe this game is kind of the only Star Wars RTS game other than Empire at War, so that makes it worth a try, I think.

The only gameplay thing other than each faction being copy-pasted I want to comment on, is that hard mode was a slog on standard campaign missions. Basically, each scenario went: 

Pause and listen to dialogue
Move to base location and build a fortress and shield generator as soon as possible
Acquire technology and resources while the AI sends units to into the meatgrinder every 30 seconds until you're ready to attack

By the time you have your fortress ready to defend your base from the endless horde, the enemy will have advanced in tech level, secured all the banthas/nerfs on the map, acquired a limitless stream of resources and have preparations to pull the rug on their own cryptocurrency scam. But the computer is as incompetent at planning as it is great at multitasking, so you'll always win in time.

Also, you'll have a white screen for the intro videos because they're an incompatible format or something, just press Esc for each one and the game will start. The videos in question are here on the store page if you want to see them.

Worth it for the campaigns, some genuinely good Star Wars lore there.
